newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Mogas down despite western hike.
newsitem.headline: Asia Naphtha/Mogas-Mogas down despite western hike.

text.p: In spite of the gasoline hikes in the west, the Singapore market was offered down by a Japanese trader on Thursday.
September gasoline prices on NYMEX continued their rally and were 0.12 cents per gallon firmer at 66.20 cents.
On Wednesday, news of an indefinite shutdown in the catalytic cracker of Exxon's Baytown, Texas refinery due to operational problems had pushed prices up 2.37 cents per gallon higher at 66.08 cents.

But in Singapore, September unleaded 95-octane was offered down to $23.10 per barrel by a Japanese trader. On Wednesday, traders had assessed levels around $23.40-$23.50 on the back of Taiwan's September tender awards.
"He must be pricing in a cargo," said a trader.
Unleaded 97-octane was in comparison, bid at $24.40 by a Dutch trader with traders assessing the differential between the 97 and 95-octane at $1.00.

The 95/92-octane spread was assessed at around 80 cents, they said, with the gasoline market still two-tiered with supplies of high-octane material tight while there were still ample supplies of low-octane.
Chinese September supplies were being offered at $2.00 per barrel and $1.75 over Singapore naphtha spot quotes, fob, for 95 and 92-octane respectively, they said.
India was rumoured to have cancelled its September buy tender for 87 RON unleaded gasoline.
The tender, for September 23-27 delivery, was scheduled to closed on Wednesday.
Naphtha resisted crude's overnight hikes and firmer tone late on Thursday with September swaps only around 10 cents per barrel firmer at $21.40/$21.55.
"Demand is pretty bad and Japan is processing more naphtha-rich crudes because middle-distillate prices are so low," said a Japanese trader.
Naphtha regional supplies were also in abundance with a prompt -- August 18-22 lifting -- 200,000-barrel full range cargo offered from Indonesia's Dumai refinery.
"There is too many barrels in the market..they can't place it," said a trader.

The bearish market was reflected in the low award into Sri Lanka's state-owned Ceylon Petroleum Corp's (CPC) sell tender for September naphtha, which was to Japanese trader Marubeni Corp at $1.42 per barrel below Singapore spot quotes, free-on- board Colombo a company official.
The next best bids were from Dutch trader Vitol and Swiss trader Glencore, both at a discount of $$1.77, he said.
The tender which offered the 125,000-barrels of chemical naphtha with a 0.65-0.72 SG cargo on a free-on-board (fob) basis from Colombo, closed August 13 and was valid for two days.

The cargo is for lifting September 3-4 after CPC had brought forward the lay dates earlier this week following a cancellation of its middle-distillate tender which occupied the earlier berthing period.

Reflecting the fundamentally weak naphtha market, the discount for the current tender is nearly three times CPC's last naphtha award for July 18-19 cargo, to Dutch trader Vitol cents per barrel below Singapore spot quotes, fob.
(Prices are in dollars per barrel)
